THE DEFECT IT MEASURED IS REPAIRED, SAME DAY, AND VERIFIED ON THE SEAT IT WAS MEASURED ON. `loop_status.next` went from 8 lines to 3 against a fresh binary with `served_by.stale: false`; the five false sentences are gone and `sync` still reports all six targets, so nothing true was suppressed.

🛑 WHAT SURVIVES THE REPAIR AND IS THE REASON THE NODE IS WORTH KEEPING. (1) THE CLASS — a per-item computation stated as a whole-system fact, invisible because every test drove exactly ONE item. Only this one rollup was examined; whether other served reports phrase per-target findings as seat-wide claims is unmeasured, and that is the sentence a later session should act on. (2) The refutation of the leading candidate: filtering scratch paths was already tried and reverted, and a 1545-node backup outside any temp path defeats it independently. (3) The method note — that the report described noise and the measurement found falsehood, and that a noise framing would have bought ranking or dedup while leaving every sentence just as untrue.

⚠️ AND ITS OWN MEASUREMENT ADVICE OUTLIVED THE FIX: the first coupling grep read `node::DECISION` as vocabulary-free, so any re-derivation must count constants, not string literals. That warning was written for a different investigation the same day and applies to this one too.

📌 NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the three standing bounds on the node-count comparison — equal counts with different ids, an edge-only divergence, and a property-only write are all still invisible. The seat-level form inherits every one of them, so this remains a reading aid and not a durability guarantee.
